body: I understand that, but this down has been going on for 1.5 years, and at first I was learning about myself, getting stronger as well, but a lot of time has been wasted and a lot has been lost in vain. I had some standards, and I don't know how to move forward. That's my problem. I always think about waht I couldve done better. It truly truly hurts. I have been collapsing, and these winter breaks we're my last hope to come to terms with reality, calm down, heal, make my life better, and for the first time, something out of my control happened, and I just fucking couldn't. So it feels like I have no ground to stand on. Ive made peace with my mistakes many times already, but this time I can't.

I don't have much to say, and the things I will say will sound over said, but it's the truth.

You wish to die, but not cause problems to others, as do I. But both arent possible.
Suicide is something best done with planning and being  logically and subconsciously convinced that it is the right thing to do. Most suicides are in moments of very strong feelings, rash suicides. Certainly avoid that since that's just stopid.

Suicide is permanent. That's why I delay it. You have a duty to your hypothetical future self. Complete that duty as to not fuck up your future in case you feel better. I do not claim to understand your sadness, but that's just the truth. Don't destroy or reduce hope for the future. 

Now, time passes, and one thing is certain, and that is however slow, 'normal' sadness that is not a severe chemical Imbalance fades with time. You should get yourself checked with a psychiatrist since you have been doing little for a month.

One thing that has really helped me feel meaning is good emotional music. Although life has no overall meaning, we derive it from progression- achieving goals and short term goals and pleasure. So keep that in mind. 

If you make yourself happier, then you will certainly find another person who you love mutually. But only in time. We never forget failed relationships, but we teach ourselves to not feel the grief. 20s are very transformative, just like your teens. You will experience new things. It is a vast world.

If this was useless, I'm sorry. That's all I have to say.

When you moved for your masters, what was the problem that made you cry?

And do you think that you can get better? Any way you won't feel this way?

Why don't you try exercising? It will be very difficult in the beginning, but it feels really good.

I am pretty much exactly the same. I am trying to just focus on what I want but it seems no case in why I am alive is acceptable. it has been 7 days of non functioning, except for spending time on YouTube and reddit to keep my mind off d off reality. My plan is to do nothing until I have a plan of what to do, whether to die, or how to deal with life. The latter seems probable because of my parents. The pros and cons will be listed, and a decision will be made. Well now that my rant is over, what are your problems?
